chunk_findings.detail: `_offered_overlap` does not implement the conflict test the change is specified to perform. The specified rule is "take an item only if `conflicts(item.globs, taken.globs, shared_globs)` is empty". The helper instead skips the comparison entirely whenever `line_key(state, other, cfg) != mine` (lines adding `if line_key(state, other, cfg) != mine: continue`), i.e. whenever the two items are on different release lines, and returns `None`. The docstring's justification ("different release lines are different branches and never collide") is an assumption about the working tree that the stated contract does not make, and the intent text never mentions a line exemption for the *offered* check (it only mentions the in-flight `item_blocker` exemption). Concrete input: `cfg` with two release lines; `slots=2`; `ready = [X(p1, globs=["src/foo.py"], line="v1"), Y(p2, globs=["src/foo.py"], line="v2")]`. Per the specified algorithm, `conflicts(X.globs, [Y].globs, shared)` is non-empty, so `plan` must offer `X` and report `Y` in `overlapped` with detail `globs overlap X (src/foo.py vs src/foo.py) offered in this plan`. With this code, `_offered_overlap` sees `line_key(Y) != line_key(X)` and returns `None`, so both `X` and `Y` are appended to `taken` and `p.ready = [X, Y]` — the offered set is *not* mutually independent, and the second claim will be refused at claim time, which is exactly the failure mode ("only 58% of offered items were mutually independent") the change exists to remove. The test suite given in the intent never mixes release lines, so none of tests (1)–(5) exercise this path and the regression is silent.

chunk_findings.detail: The new comprehension `why = {b["item"]: b["detail"] for b in out.data["blocked"]}` indexes blocked entries with `item`, but the items produced by this very `A.next_(...)` call expose their identifier as `id` (the line this hunk deletes iterates `i["id"]` over `.data["ready"]`, and the intent's detail text refers to the "<offered id>"). Given the blocked entry for the passed-over item, the comprehension raises `KeyError: 'item'`, so the test never reaches the `assert` and errors out instead of checking that the refused claim left no `reserved` reason; it must read the identifier with the same key used for ready entries (`id`).

chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes the ready items' globs from `[f"r{i}"]` to `[f"r{i:02d}/f.py"]` in a test whose stated purpose (bounded status output) has nothing to do with the new overlap rule. Under the described intent, "when no two ready items overlap the output is byte-identical to today", so a set of 40 distinct file globs should need no edit at all. The only plausible reason to rewrite them is that the new `conflicts(...)` check reports overlaps among the old values: `r1` is a string prefix of `r10`, `r2` of `r20`, etc. The replacement deliberately makes every glob the same length (zero-padded `r00`…`r39`), which removes exactly the pairs (`r1` vs `r10`, `r1/f.py` vs `r10/f.py`) that a prefix- or `commonprefix`-based overlap test would falsely flag. Concrete consequence: a `conflicts()` implementation that returns non-empty for distinct paths where one name is a prefix of another (e.g. `a.py` and `ab.py`, or `r1/f.py` and `r10/f.py`) will pass the whole new suite, because the only test that contained such adjacent names was edited to eliminate them. That is a false "conflict" reported to the user for two independent files, and no remaining test in this slice would catch it.

chunk_findings.detail: The only non-test-file behavior in this change is that `plan()` now walks `ready` and skips any item whose globs overlap an already-taken item's globs, and this diff edits the *existing* status-bound fixture from `[f"r{i}"]` to `[f"r{i:02d}/f.py"]`. Those 40 tasks are already pairwise disjoint under the old names (`r0`..`r39` are distinct single-segment paths), so under a correct overlap predicate the edit would be a no-op, and indeed the stated intent never mentions `test_status_bound.py` at all. The edit is only needed if the new overlap test conflates a glob with a path/string prefix of a *different* glob: e.g. `r1` vs `r10` (`"r10".startswith("r1")`), or in real use `src` vs `src2/util.py` or `glog` vs `glog2/x.py`. Given two independent ready items with globs `["r1"]` and `["r10"]` (patches touching disjoint paths), the new predicate reports an overlap, so the second item is pushed to `blocked` with reason `conflict` and detail "globs overlap r1 …", wasting a slot exactly like the pre-change behavior the intent says it is fixing. The fixture was renamed to two-digit directories (`r00/f.py`, `r01/f.py`) so no path is a prefix of another, which papers over the false positive instead of fixing the containment/prefix matching.
